decision_rule: If the with-skill arm does not beat the without-skill arm on assertions passed, the skill is deleted, not revised. Written before the run, per docs/adr/0003 and verbatim in intent from fe-architecture-error-handling/evals/evals.json.

assertions: States that a type alias does not create a new type - the four ID aliases are one type to the compiler.
Shows or states that passing one ID where another is expected compiles with no error.
Asks whether the IDs actually cross paths in one signature or collection before recommending branding.
Recommends branding as compile-time only, naming the zero runtime cost or the boundary cast tax.
Does not present branding as unconditionally correct.
Identifies the unit mismatch: rate 20 treated as a fraction, so applyDiscount(100,20) returns 2000.
States that the build being green tells you nothing here - the compiler checked shape, not meaning.
Attributes the root cause to Percentage being an alias for number, not a distinct type.
Notes that a brand relocates the mistake to the constructor rather than removing it.
Proposes a concrete convention fix (fraction everywhere, or explicit conversion at the boundary).

cases.concept: 3. The cutting question, both failure states
assertions: Asks whether the two types ever cross paths in one signature or collection, rather than answering brand/don't-brand directly.
Names the over-brand cost as a cast tax paid at every boundary.
Names that normalizing `as` erodes the seam - casting stops being a signal where it matters.
Distinguishes the mixing problem (compile-time) from the validation problem (runtime).
Names who pays: the teams paying assignment ceremony vs whoever made the decision.
Rejects the 'value object is just a stronger brand' framing explicitly.
Frames the choice as two different questions, not one strength ladder.
States the brand is compile-time only with zero runtime cost and enforces nothing at runtime.
States the value object is a runtime construct carrying validation, and is charged for it.
Makes the decision turn on where enforcement must sit (number of untrusted construction sites), not on which is stronger.

result.runs_per_arm_note: 1 run per arm. The 3 admissible with_skill runs went 5/5 and the deltas are 1-2 assertions on concepts whose wins are traceable to specific body lines, not to phrasing luck. Variance was not measured; a 1-assertion delta on a single run would not have been enough to decide on.

findings: Concept 2 (shape checked, not meaning) is now graded: 4/5 with skill vs 3/5 without. The smallest delta of the four cases, and the only assertion it fails is the one the body does not currently make.

The brand-relocates-the-mistake error reproduced exactly. Both the with-skill run here and the contaminated run in tasks/eval-control-arm-is-contaminated.md claimed branding fixes the unit bug, then wrote a constructor (`n as Money`) inside which the same error compiles. Two independent runs, same failure - this is a gap in the body, not run variance. IDEAS.md parks the fix; it is now admissible.

Concept 4's control failed exactly as the body predicts: it recommended the value object as a default because it 'fails closed', which is the strength-ladder belief the body overturns. Strongest evidence in this run that a body line is load-bearing.

The who-pays question is ANSWERED, against the deletion. Per the task file: if the control names the payer unprompted on t05, the deletion is confirmed. It did not. The with_skill arm did - 'every team pays assignment ceremony forever'. That clause survived the cut and did the work; the deleted decision/decider/payer slot format is not needed, but the cost clause is load-bearing.
Seam erosion (normalizing `as` stops it being a signal) appeared only in the with_skill arm. Not generic knowledge at Sonnet level.

TRIGGER GAP: the bare case-2 prompt - a code-review question with no branding vocabulary, types named Money/Percentage - did not fire the description. It is closest to trigger query t02 (money as its own type) but is phrased as 'anything wrong here?' over a code block. No query in trigger-evals.json has this shape. Worth adding to the should_trigger set.
